diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $(X,|\cdot|_X),(Y,|\cdot|_Y)$ be  Banach spaces  with the Approximation Property, i.e. we are given $\left\{\{\mathcal S}^X_\alpha\right\}_{\alpha \in A }\subset \mathcal L(X)$, $\left\{\{\mathcal S}^Y_\beta\right\}_{\beta \in B }\subset \mathcal L(Y)$ satisfying Assumption \ref{ass:approx_pro}.

issues.failure_explanation: The preceding setup and the proof of Theorem th:UAT_K_Banach use a compact-open approximating net {S^Y_beta} on the target space Y as well. Thus the advertised hypothesis is AP on both X and Y, not only on X.

failure_location.quote: via EDAs under only AP on $X$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the prose to say that the theorem requires AP on X and Y (or on the Banach spaces involved).
issues.overall_effect: The stated assumptions for the main compact-open UAT are misrepresented in the introduction.
issues.title: Compact-open UAT presented as requiring only AP on X
issues.why_classification: A one-line correction to the scope statement; the formal theorem and proof are unaffected.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $(X,<\cdot,\cdot>_X),(Y,<\cdot,\cdot>_Y)$ be separable Hilbert spaces with orthonormal bases

issues.failure_explanation: The space Y defined in the example is a standard Bochner-type Banach space built from V, H, and V*, not a Hilbert space in general. The subsequent appeal to Remark rem:HGNO_UA and HGNO/Deep-H-ONets therefore uses a false premise.

failure_location.quote: In this setup, $X,Y$ are separable Hilbert spaces

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the Hilbert claim with the correct Banach-space description and either assume AP for Y to use general EDAs, or replace Y by a genuinely Hilbert state space for which the solution map has the claimed smoothness.
issues.overall_effect: The example's claimed UA via HGNOs/Deep-H-ONets is unsupported for the stated Y.
issues.title: Navier-Stokes example claims the state space Y is Hilbert
issues.why_classification: The defect is local to an illustrative example; a contained correction or assumption restores the example without affecting the main theorems.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: $\mathcal L(X,Y)= \mathcal K(X,Y)$ for $X=\ell^p,Y= \ell^q$ for $p>q\geq 1$ (which admit Schauder bases, so they satisfy AP).

issues.failure_explanation: If L(X,Y)=K(X,Y) and the spaces have AP, then the closure of finite-rank operators A(X,Y) equals K(X,Y)=L(X,Y), so Assumption ass:propersub fails. The Pitt's theorem example therefore does not provide a counterexample to the stated assertion; at best it illustrates a case where the proper-subspace hypothesis is false.

failure_location.quote: A counterexample in the infinite-dimensional case is given by Pitt's theorem

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Rephrase the sentence to say that Pitt's theorem gives a case where A(X,Y)=L(X,Y), so Assumption ass:propersub is not satisfied, or delete the misleading 'counterexample' label.
issues.overall_effect: The remark's interpretation of Pitt's theorem is mathematically incoherent.
issues.title: Pitt's theorem misidentified as a counterexample in the proper-approximable-operator remark
issues.why_classification: This is a local correction to a remark; it does not affect the proof or statement of Theorem th:counterexample.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $\gamma\sim N(0,Q)$, $Q\in \mathcal L_1^+(X)$, Gaussian measure on a separable Hilbert space $X$
the relations there are suitably extended to the case of a Banach space $X$ under Gaussian measure $\gamma$. Therefore, in this case, Theorem \ref{th:characterization_bogachev} also holds.
Here, we take $X$ to be a Hilbert space  for simplicity.

issues.failure_explanation: The corollary states the Gaussian Sobolev UAT for a Gaussian measure on a Banach space X, but the supporting characterization theorem is proved only for separable Hilbert X. The remark invoked for the Banach extension merely asserts that the Gaussian norm identities are 'suitably extended' without proof.

failure_location.quote: Let $p\geq 1 $ and let $\mu^0$ be a Gaussian measure on  a Banach space $X$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the corollary to separable Hilbert X, or add a complete proof of the Cameron-Martin/Gaussian Sobolev norm identification and Bogachev-space inclusions for Banach X.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised Banach-space Gaussian Sobolev UAT is unsupported; only the separable Hilbert case follows from the source.
issues.title: Gaussian Sobolev UAT extended to Banach X without established norm identification
issues.why_classification: A supported resolution is to weaken the corollary to the Hilbert case, but this excludes the advertised Banach Gaussian regime; the loss is contained rather than architectural.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Assume that $X$ has the Bounded Approximation Property (BAP); that it has AP and there exists $\lambda>0$ such that $ \| {\mathcal S}_\alpha^{X}\|_{\mathcal L(X)}\leq \lambda$, for all $\alpha\in A $.
A strictly stronger property of the Bounded Approximation Property is the existence of a Schauder frame \cite{casazza2008}.

issues.failure_explanation: Standard BAP gives uniformly bounded finite-rank operators converging to the identity (strongly, or uniformly on compacts), but it does not allow one to assume the stronger nested relation S_m S_d = S_d for d<m. That relation is a basis/frame-type property, not a consequence of BAP.

failure_location.quote: Additionally, it can be assumed ${\mathcal S}^X_m {\mathcal S}^X_d={\mathcal S}^X_d,$ for all $d<m$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Delete the additional nested-operator sentence, or explicitly assume the stronger nested finite-rank condition as a separate hypothesis wherever it is actually needed.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised scope 'under BAP' is narrowed to an unintended stronger hypothesis in the assumption and in the results that cite it.
issues.title: BAP assumption falsely asserts existence of nested finite-rank approximants
issues.why_classification: The proofs shown do not appear to use the nested relation; removing it is a local correction that preserves the intended BAP-based arguments.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: An encoder (or coordinate) operator on $X$ is ${\mathcal E}^X \in \mathcal L( X , \R^{N})$
A decoder (or embedding) operator into $X$ is ${\mathcal D}^{X} \in \mathcal L( \R^{N} , X)$

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed measure identity rewrites pushforwards using set preimages under (E^X)^{-1} and (D^X)^{-1}. The encoders and decoders are arbitrary bounded linear finite-dimensional maps and are not invertible in general, so these inverses are undefined. The correct identity is the standard composition of pushforwards: (D^X)_#((E^X)_# μ) = (D^X ∘ E^X)_# μ.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the inverse-based expression with the standard pushforward composition (D^X)_#((E^X)_# \bar μ^{0:i}) = (S^X)_# \bar μ^{0:i}.
issues.overall_effect: A labelled equation used in the Sobolev membership proofs is ill-defined as written, making those proof steps unreliable until corrected.
issues.title: Pushforward identity uses inverses of non-invertible encoder/decoder maps
issues.why_classification: The correction is local and standard; the downstream estimates can proceed with the correct pushforward composition.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Since $X\ni x\mapsto  DF(x)e^{X_{\gamma}}_i\in Y$ is continuous for all $i$, we have that $G^N$ is continuous from $X$ to $\mathcal L_2(X_{\gamma},Y)$ (hence, Borel measurable) for each $N$.
with Borel measurable $D^i_{\gamma}F:X\to \mathcal L_2^i(X_\gamma,Y)$ and finite norm \eqref{eq:def_sobolev_norm_mu0_Lp_bogachev_HS}

issues.failure_explanation: The proof claims D_γF(x)=lim_N G^N(x) in L_2(X_γ,Y) for all x. The finite Gaussian Sobolev norm assumption only gives convergence of G^N(x) to D_γF(x) in L_2 for γ-a.e. x, not necessarily pointwise everywhere. The Bochner measurability argument therefore has a missing a.e. representative/extension step.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace 'for all x' by 'for γ-a.e. x' and complete the Bochner measurability argument by choosing a separable-range measurable representative on a full-measure set.
issues.overall_effect: The inclusion C^{k,p,2}_{B,γ,η}⊂D^{k,p}_γ and hence the Gaussian characterization proof are incomplete as written.
issues.title: Gaussian characterization proof asserts pointwise Bochner limit where only a.e. convergence is known
issues.why_classification: The gap is a standard measure-theoretic a.e. repair; it does not change the intended theorem or its scope.
